definition: Demanded something forcefully, not accepting refusal.
exampleSentence: The chief executive insisted that all safety protocols had been upheld.

definition: Admitted that one has committed a crime or done something wrong.
exampleSentence: The suspect confessed that he had manipulated the security logs.
The committee advocated that educational funding should be doubled.

definition: Said or did something to remove doubts or fears.
exampleSentence: The doctor reassured the family that the patient was recovering steadily.

definition: Demanded or specified a requirement, typically as part of a bargain.
exampleSentence: The contract stipulated that delivery had to take place before December.

definition: Admitted that something is true or valid after first denying it.
exampleSentence: The spokesperson conceded that delivery schedules had slipped unacceptably.

definition: Gave special importance or prominence to something in speaking.
exampleSentence: The chairperson emphasized that worker safety remained an overriding priority.

definition: Proved a statement or theory to be wrong or false.
exampleSentence: The finance ministry refuted claims of an impending austerity package.

definition: Said something again or a number of times, typically for emphasis.
exampleSentence: The foreign secretary reiterated the government's unwavering commitment to the treaty.

definition: Encouraged someone strongly to do something.
exampleSentence: Health officials urged the public to stay indoors during the blizzard.
